lessons.title: Clothes
lessons.scenario: Smarty opens his big wardrobe and shows Leo and Ana his clothes.

items.note: A shirt is a top with buttons and a collar.

image.describe: a neatly folded crisp white button-up shirt

items.note: A T-shirt is a soft casual top shaped like the letter T.

image.describe: a bright blue short-sleeved T-shirt

image.describe: a pair of neat black trousers

grammar.title: One item vs. plural clothes
grammar.explanation: Use ‘a’ with one shirt, T-shirt, or dress (‘a blue shirt’). Do not use ‘a’ with trousers or shoes—use ‘are’ (‘The shoes are red’).

practice.prompt: Which word names a top with buttons?

practice.explanation: Listen for the T sound in T-shirt.

practice.prompt: Which clothing item covers both legs?
practice.explanation: Trousers are worn on your legs.

practice.prompt: Complete the sentence.
practice.explanation: ‘A’ needs a singular noun like ‘dress’.

practice.prompt: Match each item with the right sentence.
practice.explanation: Use ‘It is’ for one T-shirt, and ‘They are’ for trousers and shoes.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence about the shoes.
practice.explanation: Shoes is plural, so use ‘are’.

practice.prompt: Choose the right verb for trousers.
practice.explanation: Trousers always takes the plural verb ‘are’.

practice.explanation: The question asks about the dress.

practice.prompt: You see a new dress and want to know its colour. What do you ask?
practice.explanation: Use ‘What colour is it?’ to ask about the colour of one thing.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.

practice.answer: He has a purple shirt and brown trousers.
options: He has a purple shirt and brown trousers.
He has a pink shirt and black trousers.
He has a white T-shirt and brown shoes.

practice.prompt: Match each item with its description.
practice.explanation: Match the colour and clothing item together.

lessons.title: I'm wearing a hat
lessons.scenario: Smarty, Mia, and Sam try on hats, jackets, and socks in the wardrobe room.

items.example: I am wearing a yellow hat.
items.note: Say ‘I am wearing…’ or ‘I’m wearing…’ to tell someone what clothes are on your body right now.

items.example: He is wearing a blue jacket.
items.note: A jacket is a short coat you wear over a shirt or T-shirt.

image.describe: a stylish blue zip-up jacket

items.note: You wear a hat on your head.

image.describe: a cheerful yellow sun hat

items.note: Socks go on your feet inside your shoes; one is a ‘sock’ and a pair is ‘socks’.

image.describe: a pair of striped green socks

grammar.title: Present continuous: am / is / are wearing
grammar.explanation: Use ‘am wearing’ for I, ‘is wearing’ for he or she, and ‘are wearing’ for you, we, or they.
examples: I am wearing a yellow hat.
She is wearing a blue jacket.

practice.prompt: What do you wear on your head?
practice.explanation: A hat goes on your head.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.audio: I am wearing a blue jacket.
practice.answer: I am wearing a blue jacket.
options: I am wearing a blue jacket.
I am wearing a yellow hat.
practice.explanation: Listen to the end of the sentence: a blue jacket.

practice.prompt: What do you wear on your feet inside your shoes?
practice.explanation: You wear socks on your feet under shoes.

practice.prompt: Complete the sentence about yourself.
practice.explanation: With ‘I’, use ‘am wearing’.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence.
practice.answer: I am wearing a yellow hat.
practice.explanation: Use ‘I am wearing’ followed by ‘a yellow hat’.

practice.prompt: Match each subject with the right form of ‘wearing’.
practice.explanation: Use am with I, is with she, and are with they.

practice.prompt: Sam wears this over his shirt. Complete the sentence.
practice.explanation: ‘A brown jacket’ is singular, matching ‘a’.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
options: Mia is wearing a white hat.
practice.explanation: Mia is wearing white socks.

practice.prompt: Complete the sentence about Smarty.
practice.explanation: Smarty is one cat (he), so use ‘is wearing’.

practice.prompt: Say the sentence aloud. You can try again.
practice.text: I'm wearing a jacket and a hat.
practice.answer: I'm wearing a jacket and a hat.
practice.explanation: ‘I’m wearing’ is the short form of ‘I am wearing’.

story.hook: What is Smarty wearing on his head and feet?

mission.setup: Smarty is showing off his outfit and wants to know what you are wearing.

turns.smarty: I am wearing a yellow hat! What are you wearing?
turns.example: I am wearing a blue T-shirt.
turns.hint: Start with I am wearing… and name a piece of clothing.

turns.smarty: Are you wearing socks?
accept: ^(?:yes|no)(?: i am wearing(?: (?:red|blue|green|yellow|black|white|pink|purple|brown))? socks| i am not wearing socks)?$
turns.example: Yes, I am wearing white socks.
turns.hint: Say Yes or No, or say I am wearing socks.

turns.smarty: Tell me about a jacket or a hat!
accept: ^(?:i am|i m|he is|she is) wearing a (?:(?:red|blue|green|yellow|black|white|pink|purple|brown) )?(?:jacket|hat)$
turns.example: I am wearing a black jacket.
turns.hint: Say I am wearing a jacket or I am wearing a hat.

lessons.title: Whose is this?
lessons.scenario: Omar and Lily find a scarf and hats on the sofa in Smarty’s room and ask who owns them.

items.example: Whose is this? It is mine.
items.note: Ask ‘Whose is this?’ when you find something and want to know who owns it.
Say ‘mine’ instead of ‘my hat’ or ‘my scarf’ when something belongs to you.
Say ‘yours’ instead of ‘your scarf’ when something belongs to the person you are talking to.

items.example: She is wearing a purple scarf.
items.note: A scarf is a long warm cloth you wear around your neck.

image.describe: a cozy purple knitted scarf

grammar.title: Whose, mine, yours
grammar.explanation: Ask ‘Whose is this?’ or ‘Whose scarf is this?’ to find the owner. Answer with ‘It is mine’ (belongs to me) or ‘It is yours’ (belongs to you).

practice.prompt: What do you wear around your neck when it is cold?
practice.explanation: A scarf keeps your neck warm.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.explanation: ‘Whose is this?’ asks who owns something.

practice.prompt: This scarf belongs to you. Complete the sentence.
practice.text: This is my scarf. It is ___.
practice.explanation: ‘My scarf’ becomes ‘mine’ when no noun follows.

practice.prompt: You are talking to Smarty about Smarty’s hat. Complete the sentence.
practice.explanation: When something belongs to the person you are talking to, say ‘yours’.

practice.prompt: Ask who owns the scarf.
practice.explanation: Put ‘Whose scarf’ first, then ‘is this?’.

practice.prompt: Match the two ways to say the same thing.
practice.explanation: Mine replaces my + noun, and yours replaces your + noun.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.explanation: Listen to the last word: mine.

practice.prompt: You find a jacket on the chair. Ask who owns it.
practice.explanation: Use ‘Whose’ before a noun to ask who owns it.

practice.prompt: Smarty hands you your book. What does Smarty say?
practice.text: Here you are! This book is ___.
practice.explanation: Smarty is giving you your own book, so Smarty says ‘yours’.

practice.prompt: Say the question and answer aloud. You can try again.
practice.text: Whose is this? It is mine.
practice.answer: Whose is this? It is mine.
practice.explanation: Ask ‘Whose is this?’ and answer ‘It is mine.’

lessons.title: Me him them
lessons.scenario: It is cold, and Smarty hands out coats and scarves to Tom, Ana, and his friends.

items.example: This blue coat is for me.
items.note: Use ‘me’ after words like ‘for’ or ‘to’ when talking about yourself.

items.example: The black hat is for him.
items.note: Use ‘him’ after words like ‘for’ or ‘to’ when talking about a boy or man.
Use ‘them’ after words like ‘for’ or ‘to’ when talking about two or more people or things.

items.example: The hot tea is for us.
items.note: Use ‘us’ after words like ‘for’ or ‘to’ when talking about you and someone else together.

items.example: She is wearing a brown coat.
items.note: A coat is a heavy outer garment you wear when it is cold.

image.describe: a warm long brown winter coat with buttons

grammar.title: Object pronouns: me, him, her, it, us, them
grammar.explanation: After words like ‘for’, use object pronouns: me (I), him (he), her (she), it (it), us (we), and them (they).

practice.prompt: What heavy item do you wear over your clothes when it is cold?
practice.explanation: A coat keeps you warm in cold weather.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.audio: This red coat is for me.
practice.answer: This red coat is for me.
options: This red coat is for me.
This red coat is for him.
This red coat is for us.
practice.explanation: Listen to the pronoun at the end: me.

practice.prompt: Tom is a boy. The scarf is for Tom. Complete the sentence.
practice.explanation: Use ‘him’ for a boy or man.

practice.prompt: Mia and Sam are two friends. The apples are for Mia and Sam.
practice.explanation: Use ‘them’ for two or more people.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence about you and your friend together.
practice.explanation: Use ‘us’ when you are included in the group.

practice.prompt: Match each subject pronoun with its object pronoun.
practice.explanation: I → me, he → him, we → us, they → them.

practice.prompt: Ana is a girl. Complete the sentence about Ana.
practice.explanation: Use ‘her’ for a girl or woman.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.audio: The blue hats are for them.
practice.answer: The blue hats are for them.
options: The blue hats are for them.
The blue hats are for us.
The blue hat is for him.
practice.explanation: Listen to the end: for them.

practice.prompt: Smarty is a cat. Complete the sentence about the cat.
practice.explanation: Use ‘it’ for an animal or thing.

practice.prompt: Say the sentence aloud. You can try again.
practice.text: This brown coat is for me.
practice.answer: This brown coat is for me.
practice.explanation: Use ‘me’ after ‘for’ when talking about yourself.

lessons.scenario: Smarty and his friends get ready for a fashion show in the wardrobe room.

items.note: Say ‘I want…’ when you wish to have or wear something.

items.note: Say ‘favourite’ for the one thing you like best of all.

grammar.explanation: Combine colour words and clothes after ‘I am wearing’ or ‘I want’ to describe a complete outfit.
examples: I am wearing a red coat and black boots.
I want my favourite blue hat.

practice.prompt: Which tall footwear covers your ankles?

episode.title: The Key in the Red Coat

panels.speaker: Smarty
panels.text: I am wearing my favourite red coat and black boots!

image.describe: Smarty the black cat smiling in a bright red coat and shiny black boots in his wardrobe room.

panels.speaker: Mia
panels.text: What colour is your scarf, Smarty?

image.describe: Mia the cat pointing to two folded scarves—one yellow and one blue—on a table.

panels.speaker: Smarty
panels.text: It is yellow! This yellow scarf is for me, and the blue scarf is for you.

panels.speaker: Sam
panels.text: Whose hat is this on the chair?

image.describe: Sam the cat holding up a brown hat next to a wooden chair.

panels.speaker: Smarty
panels.text: It is mine! What is in my red coat?

panels.speaker: Mia
panels.text: It is a small green key!

image.describe: Smarty the black cat holding a shiny small green key pulled from his red coat.

panels.speaker: Sam
panels.text: There is a big purple box under the bed!

panels.speaker: Smarty
panels.text: This key is for that box! What is in the purple box?

image.describe: Smarty, Mia, and Sam peeking under the bed at a mysterious big locked purple box while Smarty holds the green key.
